modules.title: Beginner SQL Foundations
modules.description: Master relational database basics, SELECT projections, WHERE filtering, ordering, and aggregation.

lessons.title: Introduction to Relational Databases & SELECT
lessons.concept: A relational database organizes data into tables consisting of rows and columns. The SELECT statement retrieves columns from a table.
lessons.expectedOutput: List of student IDs and their corresponding names.
lessons.exercisePrompt: Write a query to retrieve all columns from the students table.
hints: Use the asterisk (*) symbol to select all columns.
Make sure to specify FROM students;

lessons.title: Filtering Records with WHERE & Comparison Operators
lessons.concept: The WHERE clause filters records based on boolean conditions such as =, >, <, >=, <=, and <>.
lessons.syntax: SELECT column1 FROM table_name WHERE condition;
lessons.example: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE marks >= 80;
lessons.exercisePrompt: Find all students who have marks strictly greater than 75.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE marks > 75;

lessons.title: Sorting and Limiting with ORDER BY & LIMIT
lessons.concept: ORDER BY sorts the returned records in ASC (ascending) or DESC (descending) order. LIMIT restricts the number of rows returned.
lessons.syntax: SELECT column1 FROM table_name ORDER BY column1 DESC LIMIT n;
lessons.example: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC LIMIT 3;
lessons.exercisePrompt: Select the top 2 students sorted alphabetically by name.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT name FROM students ORDER BY name ASC LIMIT 2;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT name FROM students ORDER BY name ASC LIMIT 2;

modules.title: Joins, Aggregations & Subqueries
modules.description: Connect related tables with INNER and LEFT JOINs, calculate summary metrics with GROUP BY and HAVING.

lessons.title: Connecting Tables with INNER JOIN
lessons.concept: An INNER JOIN selects records that have matching values in both tables based on a foreign key relationship.
lessons.syntax: SELECT t1.col, t2.col FROM table1 t1 INNER JOIN table2 t2 ON t1.id = t2.ref_id;
lessons.example: SELECT s.name, c.title FROM students s INNER JOIN enrolments e ON s.id = e.student_id INNER JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id;
lessons.expectedOutput: Student names paired with the title of each course they are taking.
lessons.exercisePrompt: Select student name and their enrolment term by joining students and enrolments.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT s.name, e.term FROM students s INNER JOIN enrolments e ON s.id = e.student_id;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT s.name, e.term FROM students s INNER JOIN enrolments e ON s.id = e.student_id;

lessons.title: Summarizing Data with GROUP BY & HAVING
lessons.concept: GROUP BY aggregates rows that have the same values into summary rows. HAVING filters groups after aggregation.
lessons.syntax: SELECT category, COUNT(*), AVG(val) FROM table GROUP BY category HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
lessons.example: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(salary) as avg_sal FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;
lessons.expectedOutput: Number of employees and average salary per department.
lessons.exercisePrompt: List department_id and average salary for departments with average salary above 80000.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) as avg_sal FROM employees GROUP BY department_id HAVING AVG(salary) > 80000;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) as avg_sal FROM employees GROUP BY department_id HAVING AVG(salary) > 80000;

lessons.title: Subqueries and Nested Expressions
lessons.concept: A subquery is a query nested inside another query, used in WHERE clauses or column projections.
lessons.syntax: SELECT col FROM table WHERE val > (SELECT AVG(val) FROM table);
lessons.example: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);
lessons.expectedOutput: Employees whose salary is higher than the overall company average.
lessons.exercisePrompt: Find employees who earn more than the overall average salary.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);
hints: Use (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees) as the comparator in the WHERE clause.

modules.title: Advanced SQL & Performance
modules.description: Common Table Expressions (CTEs), Window Functions, Indexing strategies, and Transactions.

lessons.title: Common Table Expressions (WITH Clause)
lessons.concept: Common Table Expressions (CTEs) define temporary named result sets that can be referenced within a SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE statement.
lessons.syntax: WITH cte_name AS (SELECT ...) SELECT * FROM cte_name;
lessons.example: WITH HighSpenders AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(total_cents) as spent FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT * FROM HighSpenders WHERE spent > 50000;
lessons.expectedOutput: Customers who have spent more than $500 total.
lessons.exercisePrompt: Create a CTE to calculate total order revenue per customer.
lessons.starterSql: WITH CustomerRevenue AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(total_cents) as revenue FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT * FROM CustomerRevenue;
lessons.solutionSql: WITH CustomerRevenue AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(total_cents) as revenue FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT * FROM CustomerRevenue;
hints: Query the CTE with SELECT * FROM CustomerRevenue;

lessons.title: Window Functions (RANK, ROW_NUMBER)
lessons.concept: Window functions perform calculations across a set of table rows that are related to the current row, without collapsing rows like GROUP BY.
lessons.syntax: SELECT col, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) FROM employees;
lessons.example: SELECT name, salary, department_id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) as rank FROM employees;
lessons.expectedOutput: Employees ranked by salary within their respective departments.
lessons.exercisePrompt: Select employee name, salary and row number ordered by salary descending.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT name, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) as row_num FROM employees;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT name, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) as row_num FROM employees;
hints: Use ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC)

lessons.title: Transactions & ACID Guarantees
lessons.concept: Transactions bundle multiple database operations into an atomic unit with COMMIT and ROLLBACK.
lessons.example: BEGIN TRANSACTION; UPDATE products SET stock_quantity = stock_quantity - 1 WHERE id = 1; COMMIT;
lessons.exercisePrompt: Inspect product inventory and simulate atomic stock verification.
lessons.starterSql: SELECT id, title, stock_quantity FROM products WHERE stock_quantity > 0;
lessons.solutionSql: SELECT id, title, stock_quantity FROM products WHERE stock_quantity > 0;
hints: Verify product stock before executing checkout transactions.

challenges.title: High Honor Roll Students
challenges.description: Find all students who scored above 85 marks. Return name and marks ordered from highest marks to lowest marks.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE marks > 85 ORDER BY marks DESC;

challenges.title: Library Book Catalogue
challenges.description: Select the id and title of all books in the library catalogue, sorted alphabetically by title.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT id, title FROM books ORDER BY ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT id, title FROM books ORDER BY title ASC;
hints: Select id and title from books
Sort with ORDER BY title ASC

challenges.title: Course Enrolment Roster
challenges.description: List each student's name, the title of the course they are enrolled in, and the enrolment term. Order by student name ascending, then course title ascending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT s.name, c.title, e.term FROM students s ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT s.name, c.title, e.term FROM students s INNER JOIN enrolments e ON s.id = e.student_id INNER JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id ORDER BY s.name ASC, c.title ASC;
hints: Join students with enrolments on s.id = e.student_id
Order by s.name ASC, c.title ASC

challenges.title: Top Earners by Department
challenges.description: Find all employees who have a salary of 75000 or greater and belong to a non-null department. Return name, salary, and department_id ordered by salary descending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT name, salary, department_id FROM employees WHERE ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT name, salary, department_id FROM employees WHERE salary >= 75000 AND department_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY salary DESC;

challenges.title: Customer Order Revenue
challenges.description: Calculate each ordering customer's total expenditure in dollars from order_items (quantity * unit_price_cents / 100.0). Return customer name and total_spent rounded to 2 decimal places, ordered by total_spent descending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT c.name, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price_cents) / 100.0, 2) AS total_spent FROM customers c ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT c.name, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price_cents) / 100.0, 2) AS total_spent FROM customers c INNER JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id INNER JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY total_spent DESC;

challenges.title: Open & Unreturned Loans
challenges.description: List all active loans where returned_on IS NULL. Return member name, book title, and loaned_on date, ordered by loaned_on ascending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT m.name, b.title, l.loaned_on FROM loans l ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT m.name, b.title, l.loaned_on FROM loans l INNER JOIN members m ON l.member_id = m.id INNER JOIN books b ON l.book_id = b.id WHERE l.returned_on IS NULL ORDER BY l.loaned_on ASC;
hints: Join loans with members and books

challenges.title: Affordable Store Products
challenges.description: Find all products priced under 2000 cents ($20.00). Return name and price_cents ordered from lowest price to highest.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT name, price_cents FROM products WHERE ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT name, price_cents FROM products WHERE price_cents < 2000 ORDER BY price_cents ASC;
hints: Sort with ORDER BY price_cents ASC

challenges.title: Top-Level Managers
challenges.description: Find all employees who do not report to any manager (manager_id IS NULL). Return id, name, and salary ordered by salary descending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT id, name, salary FROM employees WHERE ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT id, name, salary FROM employees WHERE manager_id IS NULL ORDER BY salary DESC;
hints: Use IS NULL (not = NULL) to check manager_id

challenges.title: Department Headcount & Average Salary
challenges.description: For every department (including departments with zero employees), return department name, headcount, and average salary rounded to 2 decimal places. Order by headcount descending, then department name ascending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT d.name, COUNT(e.id) AS headcount, ROUND(AVG(e.salary), 2) AS avg_salary FROM departments d ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT d.name, COUNT(e.id) AS headcount, ROUND(AVG(e.salary), 2) AS avg_salary FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.id, d.name ORDER BY headcount DESC, d.name ASC;
hints: Use LEFT JOIN so departments without employees are included
Use COUNT(e.id) instead of COUNT(*) so empty departments show 0

challenges.title: Books and Their Authors
challenges.description: Return each book's title alongside its author's name (aliased as author_name), sorted alphabetically by book title.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT b.title, a.name AS author_name FROM books b ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT b.title, a.name AS author_name FROM books b INNER JOIN authors a ON b.author_id = a.id ORDER BY b.title ASC;
hints: Join books with authors on b.author_id = a.id

challenges.title: Unenrolled Students
challenges.description: Find all students who are not enrolled in any course yet. Return id, name, and marks ordered by id ascending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT s.id, s.name, s.marks FROM students s ...
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT s.id, s.name, s.marks FROM students s LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON s.id = e.student_id WHERE e.student_id IS NULL ORDER BY s.id ASC;
hints: Use LEFT JOIN enrolments e ON s.id = e.student_id
Filter with WHERE e.student_id IS NULL

challenges.title: Above-Average Earners
challenges.description: Using a subquery, find all employees whose salary is strictly greater than the company-wide average salary. Return name and salary ordered by salary descending.
challenges.starterSql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (...)
challenges.solutionSql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees) ORDER BY salary DESC;
